reviews.review: Can we have some ducking multiplayer?

The "Single-Player Tarkov" you never knew you needed, featuring 100% more feathers and 100% less Gear Fear.

Escape From Duckov is a brilliant example of how to take a hardcore, stressful genre and make it approachable without losing its "bite." While the name is a clear nod to Escape From Tarkov, this top-down extraction shooter stands entirely on its own two webbed feet. By removing the soul-crushing PvP element, Team Soda has created a tactical sandbox where you can actually take your time to appreciate the mechanics. The gameplay loop is incredibly tight: you drop into one of the five diverse maps, scavenge for everything from scrap metal to "bread crumbs," and fight off hostile duck factions in intense, high-stakes gunfights. It captures that "one more raid" feeling perfectly, making it the ultimate "no-brainer" game for anyone who wants the thrill of an extraction shooter without the toxicity of a competitive lobby.

The depth of the progression system is where the game truly hides its complexity. Your bunker isn't just a menu; it’s a living base that you can customize and upgrade with furniture and crafting stations. The weapon customization is surprisingly detailed—you can spend hours in your hideout tweaking attachments and ammo types for your favorite "Quack-47" or "Duck-19." Watching your base grow from a damp hole into a high-tech fortress inhabited by a quirky cast of NPC ducks like Jeff and Xiaoming gives the game a sense of heart and personality that its grit-and-grime inspirations often lack. It’s a game that respects your time by letting you choose your own difficulty, making it as "chill" or as "hardcore" as you want your Friday night to be.

The only real hurdle is the mid-game grind. Around the 20-hour mark, you’ll find that some of the base upgrades and research projects require a staggering amount of currency and rare RNG loot. Because it’s a single-player game, having to wait real-time minutes for research or farming the same boss for a specific "Golden Egg" component can occasionally feel like a bit of a drag. However, the recent 2026 updates and the robust Steam Workshop support have done a lot to smooth this out, offering mods that can tweak the economy to your liking. If you can push through the occasional resource wall, the ending provides a genuinely satisfying (and surprisingly emotional) closure to Flux’s journey. It’s a must-play indie gem that proves you don't need a massive budget—just a good pun and a lot of ducks.

9/10 — I lost all my gear because I got greedy for a piece of toast, and I’ve never been happier. Quack.
